Choosing a backpack for daily commuting

A commuting backpack has to do three jobs at once: carry a laptop safely, stay comfortable for an hour of walking, and survive years of being dropped under desks. Start by measuring your laptop and add two centimetres in each direction.

Look at the shoulder straps first. Wide, padded straps spread the weight, and a chest strap stops the bag from swinging when you hurry. A back panel with firm foam keeps hard objects from pressing into your spine.

Fabric weight is the next thing to check. Thick polyester or nylon with a water-resistant coating handles light rain, and taped seams keep the inside dry for longer. Zips should be large and run smoothly in both directions.

Finally, think about organisation. One main compartment, one padded sleeve and two small pockets are plenty. More pockets mean more weight and more places to lose keys.
